places.ref: A Deep Dive into the Gospels
places.say: Four writers, four audiences, one empty tomb. The differences mark real witnesses.
Written for us, not to us. Not every command in the Gospels is aimed at you.

places.ref: The Historical Witness of John's Gospel
places.say: A real eyewitness wrote so you'd believe. "Lord and God" likely answers Caesar's own title.
John tells you why he wrote: "so that you may believe." The whole book builds that case.
John starts where others would finish: the eternal Word, who is God, became flesh.
God couldn't wave sin away without denying who he is, so he came and paid for it himself.
Asked who he was, John the Baptist kept saying no. He was the voice pointing to Jesus.
Every prophet was a shadow. The promise was always heading for Jesus.
John the Baptist didn't recognize the Messiah until the Spirit came down and stayed.

places.ref: The Calling of the First Disciples
places.say: Following Jesus starts with "come and see," passed from one ordinary person to the next.
Water meant for ritual washing becomes the best wine, and far more than anyone needed.
He took time to braid the whip. He deliberately reclaimed the one place outsiders could pray.
A faith someone handed you isn't yours until you take it to God yourself.
We're told to be baptized, but if salvation depends on anything you do, the cross wasn't enough.
Told the crowds were going to Jesus, John the Baptist kept baptizing and called his joy complete.
Everything said this conversation shouldn't happen. Jesus sat down anyway and offered living water: the Spirit.

places.ref: He Took Him at His Word
places.say: The father walked home on Jesus's word alone. That's not blind faith; God keeps his promises.
A man walks after 38 years, and all the leaders can see is the mat he's carrying.
Whoever makes a thing says what it's for. Healing on the Sabbath claimed the day as his.

places.ref: The Feeding of the Five Thousand
places.say: The God who fed his people before feeds them again, and they still miss who he is.
John barely tells the walk on water. He wants your eyes on the bread.

places.ref: I AM — Answering the Burning Bush
places.say: Jesus did claim to be God, in two words from the burning bush: "I am."
Not a bread of life. The bread of life. What every life leans on comes from him alone.
Many walked away over a hard teaching. Jesus didn't panic. He knew from the beginning.
Even his brothers told him to go prove himself. He went on his own clock, without a show.

places.ref: The Miracle or the Miracle Worker
places.say: Believing because you saw a miracle is fragile. Is your faith in the miracle or the miracle worker?

places.ref: The Day They Did Not Pour the Water
places.say: On the one day no water was poured: "If anyone is thirsty, come to me."

places.ref: The Story John Did Not Write
places.say: John probably didn't write this story, but it happened. Jesus neither condemns the woman nor excuses her.

places.ref: I Am the Light of the World
places.say: The light is for everyone, so no one inherits it. You have to walk in it.
"Before Abraham was, I am." The men who heard him understood, and picked up stones.
Suffering isn't a scoreboard. Stop asking who sinned; ask what you'll do with it.
